brief: BTIG's technical strategist contrasts market internals around the September FOMC meeting with those at the July meeting. In July, fear was elevated (10-day put/call ratios near yearly highs) but breadth was healthy (over 70% of SPX names above their 200 DMA), so BTIG called an end to the momentum unwind and looked for a tactical bounce, consistent with SPX gaining 1%+ on the Thursday after each of the last three FOMC meetings. Heading into today's meeting, the picture flipped: anecdotal client and media sentiment expected a rally on a hike, put/call ratios sat near yearly lows, yet breadth deteriorated to 49% of SPX names above their 200 DMA, the first sub-50% reading since April 2000 while SPX stayed within 4% of an all-time high. Because strength isn't being rewarded, more stocks are breaking their 200 DMAs (financials, industrials, transports, hotels), and 10-year real rates hit fresh multi-year highs. BTIG says the correction needs less complacency, more oversold conditions and a higher-correlation decline before it runs its course, and continues to see downside risk.
